b: The next day at about three in the morning the bus dropped us off and left.. Now we had to go to a place called Ha Long Bay.. They'd arranged it with an agent.. But that bus would only come at half past seven.. Until then we had to stand, or sit, on the road

So with our bags and bundles we lay on a bench on the street.. That's when my problem started.. My bladder fills up often.. Having grown up in Colombo, I'm not in the habit of slipping off to the roadside.. I need a Western toilet..And it's a communist country too .. If I slip behind a tree somewhere, get caught on camera and disappear, who'll find me.. These ones would run back to Colombo the next second

Somehow I found a toilet on Google and took Dhanush along for company.. Three in the morning.. Not even many street lights.. The silence of a graveyard.. In a park next to a government building I saw the letters WC and ran happily, and they'd locked it with a huge Dindigul padlock.. Heartbroken, I came back.. But even in that pitch darkness two women had set up a speaker box and were happily singing along to their songs.. They didn't have a drop of fear… Even seeing us, they didn't think twice.. If it were back home, a thousand people would have said things and we'd have shut them up at home.. I felt proud seeing them… The freedom Gandhi dreamed of was there in Vietnam… I'll tell you about this in detail in another chapter
Soon I couldn't hold it again, and I took Sing Keeth along to look at another place.. Otherwise I'd surely have got lost.. Without a word about my nagging, he came along patiently

Walking ten minutes and asking a street sweeper, I reached the place… Only after I'd peacefully relieved nature's call did life come back into me.. As we walked back, the city had just started coming to life..Like back home, everyone had started their morning walks with their dogs..Then, as someone there slipped behind a tree, everyone glared at me.. Their ears would have bled from my half-hour lecture on it being a communist country .. Glad they only glared

Dawn broke and the light started to come.. The shops started opening too… If we lay outside like this, people would look at us with disgust, so we tried to get into a shop.. The poor thing, it was a young boy's shop we got.. Like the story of giving the camel's head a shelter, we took over the whole place with our bags and bundles.. Seems the boy's mother was the shop owner; she kept glaring at the boy

Meanwhile this Sing Keeth, needing to change money, went looking for gold shops and dragged me along..We went in and out shop after shop and somehow changed it, and by the time we came back the bus had come too
note: Dindigul in Tamil Nadu is famous for its huge, strong padlocks. Gandhi said India would be truly free when a woman could walk alone at midnight. In the fable, a camel given shelter for its head ends up taking over the whole tent.
